records.name: The Stagecrafters Theater
records.summary: A community theater company in Chestnut Hill that stages five shows a season. Anyone can buy tickets, audition, volunteer, or join as a member.
records.what_you_do: Audition by appointment, volunteer on stage or behind the scenes with no theater experience needed, or join as a member. Tickets and season subscriptions are also sold to the public.

schedule.text: Five shows each season. Audition forms for each production are posted about one month before its auditions.

cost.text: Single tickets are sold per show. A 2026 to 2027 season subscription for all five shows is $85. The site says annual membership dues cost the same as a subscription.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Chestnut Hill West line, Chestnut Hill station, which the theater's directions page calls a short walk. Riders who need mobility help can be dropped off at the theater before the driver parks. The theater sits toward the rear of the property, up a short driveway.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer Interest Form on the volunteer page, or email volunteer@thestagecrafters.org with questions.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no previous theater experience is necessary and that staff help place new volunteers. The join page says the company casts shows from the community, including first-time actors.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers help with lights and sound, building sets, costumes, ushering and ticketing, and marketing, and no theater background is needed. The page does not say how many hours a volunteer gives, so ask the volunteer address before your first shift. Auditions are by appointment, and performers send a headshot and resume after choosing a slot.
first_visit_tips: Park on the street nearby. The page says on-street parking is usually free during most performances, but you cannot park on theater property during a show.
Watch for the audition form that goes up about a month before each show's auditions.
Email the volunteer address with questions about time commitment before you come, since the page does not give it.
Membership asks for four meetings a year (at least two to keep voting rights) and at least one volunteer shift a year.

records.notes: The volunteer page gives no time commitment, background check or service hours policy. The membership page gives no dollar amount for dues, so the $85 subscription price is carried over from tier 1.

records.name: The Stained Glass Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings stained glass to Philadelphia public high school students and also teaches stained glass workshops at its studio on South Broad Street.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a stained glass workshop, which usually runs 2 to 4 hours, and make a small piece from a pre-designed pattern, such as a sun catcher or ornament. Volunteer through the Volunteer Interest Form, where no stained glass experience is needed. Families can also use the Interest Form to express interest in the student program for the 2026 to 2027 school year.

schedule.text: Multi-week classes and workshops are listed on the classes page. The page shows no dates or times, and each class has its own listing page. The student program meets weekly after school.

cost.text: Each workshop listed on the classes page costs $150. The student program is free, and the group says its materials, instruction, transportation help, and meals cost students nothing.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Broad Street Line to Lombard-South station, then a short walk north. Bus routes 4, 27, 32, 40, 45, 47 and 57 stop within a block or two of the studio.

first_step.how: Pick a workshop on the classes page and sign up through its listing. Email windowsthatopendoors@gmail.com with questions; the group says replies take 24 to 48 hours.
first_step.basis: The classes page says no experience is needed unless a listing says otherwise, and that most workshops suit beginners. It also gives an email address for questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workshop usually runs 2 to 4 hours, and you leave with a small piece such as a sun catcher, an ornament, or a simple panel made from a pre-set pattern. Most workshops suit beginners, so you do not need to bring any skill. Each listed workshop costs $150.
first_visit_tips: Wear closed-toe shoes and long pants, and avoid loose sleeves or dangling items.
Bring only a closable water bottle, since no food is allowed in the studio.
Street parking is limited, so allow extra time, or use a nearby garage or the Broad Street Line.
Volunteers can use the Volunteer Interest Form on the Get Involved page, and no stained glass experience is needed.

records.notes: Tier 1 said workshop fees help fund the student program. Neither the home page nor the about page says so (the about page says the student program is free), so that claim was removed. The FAQ page returned a 404 and was not used. The get-involved page also names Woodmere Art Museum as a second site for the student program; no address was shown, so it is not added as a location. The closest interest tag for stained glass is craft_circle.

records.name: The Thread
records.summary: A free art installation in Vernon Park in Germantown. Visitors can use a disconnected rotary phone to leave a message about grief, healing, or someone they have lost, and recordings may be kept in a project archive.
records.what_you_do: Visit the disconnected rotary phone in Vernon Park, or call the project's phone line to leave a message for someone you have lost or share a grief or healing story for the archive. You can also sign up for news by email.

schedule.text: Open daily, with no set hours listed.

first_step.how: Visit the rotary phone at Vernon Park, which is open daily, or call (267) 314-7161 to leave a story.
first_step.basis: The park is free and open daily, and anyone can take part by visiting or calling. The site describes no group to join, so there is no meeting and no sign-up step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visiting Vernon Park at 5800 Germantown Ave is a quiet, reflective stop with a disconnected rotary phone you can use to leave a message for someone you have lost. You can also call the project's phone line to share a grief or healing story, and the project may keep and publicly share recordings through its archive. Visiting the park costs nothing, and the site lists no set hours.
first_visit_tips: The Thread is not a helpline. The site points to its Resources page for other support.
Submitting a recording gives The Thread permission to keep, edit, and publicly share it, so think first about what you say.
The park is open daily, and the site lists no set hours.

records.notes: The events page lists past events from 2023 through January 2026, and only one of them is in 2026. The site does not confirm that the rotary phone or the phone line is working right now.

records.name: The Village of Arts and Humanities
records.summary: A community arts and youth organization on Germantown Avenue in North Philadelphia. It runs youth arts and farm education, a media lab, and neighborhood projects with young people and local residents.
records.what_you_do: Call or email to ask about the youth studios (music production, dance, fashion design, ceramics, photography, and graphic design) or the Philly Earth farm classes for ages 9 to 19. You can also take part in a neighborhood project or sign up for the newsletter. The site lists no volunteer openings.

schedule.text: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 10 am to 5 pm. Philly Earth farm classes run after school and in summer. The site does not list meeting days or times for its youth studios.

locations.label: The Village of Arts and Humanities

cost.text: The Village Youth page calls its arts education free and mentions paid creative opportunities for young people. Philly Earth class costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Call 215-225-7830 or email info@villagearts.org to ask about the next Philly Earth farm class or a Village Youth studio, including ages and start dates.
first_step.basis: The youth pages name the studios and farm classes and give office hours and a phone line, but describe no enrollment steps. The only way in is to call or email, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Philly Earth classes run after school and in summer for ages 9 to 19. Students learn composting, companion planting, and simple builds such as rocket stoves and rainwater collection, and they can earn sustainability badges. The site does not say how long a class lasts or what it costs, so call the office first.
first_visit_tips: Call the office on a weekday between 10 am and 5 pm, since those are the listed office hours.
Ask about the age range and the start date, since the farm page lists ages 9 to 19 and no start date.
The farm classes are taught on the teaching farm on the Village campus at 2544 Germantown Ave.

records.notes: The Village Youth page gives no age range; the 9 to 19 range comes from the Philly Earth page, which is dated July 28, 2023. The Village Youth page is dated October 1, 2024. The newest dated item is the join page, published March 28, 2025. The site has no access details, so none are recorded.

records.name: The Welcome Church
records.summary: A small church community on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway that welcomes all people, especially people experiencing homelessness. It holds an outdoor service on certain Sundays, and it collects winter clothing and makes bag lunches.
records.what_you_do: Come to Church on Logan, the outdoor service at Aviator Park on the first and last Sunday of each month, and stay for the coffee hour. You can also help make bag lunches on certain Mondays, or donate winter items.

schedule.text: Church on Logan meets outdoors at Aviator Park on the first and last Sunday of each month at 3 pm, regardless of weather, with a coffee hour afterward. A Tuesday gathering runs from noon to 3:30 pm at 2111 Sansom Street, with Bible study from 1:30 pm.

locations.label: Aviator Park, across from the Franklin Institute (Church on Logan)
Tuesday gathering at Lutheran Church of the Holy Communion

cost.text: Cost is not listed for worship or the coffee hour.

first_step.how: Come to Church on Logan at Aviator Park on the first or last Sunday of the month at 3 pm, then stay for the coffee hour.
first_step.basis: The About Us page gives a fixed outdoor time and place, a coffee hour afterward, and a named contact, and the presbytery page says all are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The service is held outdoors and goes ahead regardless of the weather, so dress for it. After the service, coffee hour hosts from different congregations walk around the park offering snacks.
first_visit_tips: Email Rev. Schaunel Steinnagel at rvschaunel@aol.com or call 302-463-0542 to confirm the next service date, since it falls only on the first and last Sunday.
The church's winter needs list includes knit hats, gloves, hand warmers, and blankets, if you want to bring something to donate.
The Tuesday gathering at 2111 Sansom Street runs from noon to 3:30 pm, with Bible study from 1:30 pm.

records.notes: The About Us page is undated. The 2026 evidence (winter needs and documents dated February 2026) is on the presbytery page. The church does not use the word volunteer; its contact page says visitors reach a pastor through the contact form. Tier 1 had last_sign_of_life as the bare year 2026; corrected to 2026-02. The summary no longer mentions meal drives, which the site does not describe.

records.name: The Why Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit, founded in 2021, that runs media and animation studios and a free after-school digital media lab. A math and building series is listed as coming soon.
records.what_you_do: Book a session of the After School Digital Media Labs through the Program Sign-Up page. Summer media and animation studios and an English and language arts in animation program are listed, but the site shows no dates for them. You can volunteer through the Volunteer page, which links to a VolunteerMatch listing.

schedule.text: Summer media and animation studios run in summer, but the site shows no dates. The After School Digital Media Labs run in sessions of 2 hours, and you pick a day on the booking calendar.

cost.text: The After School Digital Media Labs are listed under free neighborhood programs. The site shows no cost for the summer studios.

first_step.how: Book a session of the After School Digital Media Labs on the Program Sign-Up page, or email info@thewhyproject.org to ask about the summer studios.
first_step.basis: The labs can be booked online and are listed as free, so anyone can ask to join. The summer studios show no dates or ages on the site, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each After School Digital Media Lab session runs 2 hours and covers videography, music mixing, instrumentation, animation, and production. You choose a day on the booking calendar on the sign-up page. The site does not list ages, group size, or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Use the booking calendar on the Program Sign-Up page to pick a session day.
Email info@thewhyproject.org or call (215) 395-5343 to ask about ages and summer studio dates.
The only address the site shows is 602 S 52nd Street.

records.notes: The Summer Media Studio page is dated only Summer 2024, with no month, so it is not used as a last sign of life. probably_active rests on the working booking calendar and no dated page after 2024; a reviewer should check this. The Mathematics Through Building page is marked coming soon, so it is not listed as an offered program. The volunteer page's Start Now button leads to a third-party VolunteerMatch listing, which was not read.

records.name: The Woodlands Trust for Historic Preservation
records.summary: A historic cemetery and garden at 4000 Woodland Avenue. It runs public tours, a public events calendar, and volunteer work days where people clean paths, plant and care for trees, and help welcome visitors.
records.what_you_do: Book a tour of the mansion and cemetery ($20 a person), join a public event such as a walk or an evening event, or sign up for a clean-up or tree day. The Grave Gardeners program, run by The Woodlands, opens applications each January on its own site and is limited to 150 gardeners.

schedule.text: The grounds are open every day from dawn until dusk. Public tours run on weekdays from April through October and last about 1.5 hours. Clean-up work days are on weekends from October to March and on weekday evenings from April to September. Public events are listed on the events calendar.

cost.text: Tours are $20 per person, and a space to eat lunch adds $5 per person. Individual membership is $40 a year and brings invitations to members-only events, discounts on ticketed events, and occasional after-dark access. Other event prices vary.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Subway-Surface Trolley to the 40th Street Trolley Portal at 40th and Woodland, directly across from the gates (any line except T1). Paved roads, historic brick sidewalks, and grass, with most roads having a 4-inch curb. The one ADA restroom is at the northeast corner of the Stable and is open when staff are on site and during public events. A wedge ramp for event areas can be set up with advance notice. Hamilton Mansion has four steps, and a ramp can be added on request. An event space accessibility map is available.

first_step.how: Book a tour on the tours page at least 2 weeks ahead, or walk the grounds yourself during open hours.
first_step.basis: The grounds and public events are open to anyone, and tours are booked by form, phone, or email. The volunteer page says to contact the group or join its mailing list, but it gives no sign-up form.
first_step.what_to_expect: A tour takes about 1.5 hours on a weekday from April to October, costs $20 per person, and needs a booking at least 2 weeks ahead with a 50 percent deposit. It covers the cemetery and the Hamilton Mansion, which is open only for appointments or certain events. The cemetery still holds funerals, so a service can change your tour plans on short notice.
first_visit_tips: Book at least 2 weeks ahead. A 50 percent deposit holds the tour and is refundable up to 5 days before.
Take the SEPTA trolley to 40th and Woodland. The gates are directly across from the trolley portal.
Plan to leave before sunset, since safety staff close the gates each evening.
Children under 14 need an adult with them, and dogs must stay on a leash at all times.

records.notes: The visit page's trolley closure notice has no year, so it is not recorded. The volunteer page names no general sign-up form, age minimum, service hours letter, or background check; training is described only for tour guide candidates. The events calendar lists Oct 2026 events, including a members-only party on Oct 29, 2026.

notes: Seven records written, all as a tier 2 deep pass. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used (search used only for The Welcome Church Sunday time, then verified by fetching its About Us page). 30 WebFetch calls used, at most 6 per group. One FAQ page (Stained Glass Project) returned 404 and was not counted as blocked. Corrections to tier 1: (1) The Stained Glass Project summary no longer says workshop fees fund the student program, which the group's pages do not say. (2) The Welcome Church last_sign_of_life was a bare year; now 2026-02, and the Sunday service is now recorded as the first and last Sunday outdoor service at 3 pm (Church on Logan) instead of a weekly Sunday service. (3) The Why Project math series is marked coming soon, and the summary says so. (4) The Village of Arts schedule days (Monday to Friday) were office hours, so they moved into the text. Not written up as records: Woodmere Art Museum (student program site, no address seen), Lutheran Church of the Holy Communion (Tuesday gathering host, no URL seen; its address is in the Welcome Church record), Green Philly and Philly Queer Birders (partners on the Woodlands calendar, no URLs seen), and Grave Gardeners (a program of The Woodlands, at gravegardeners.org, not fetched). Process error to report: I made one call to a Claude Docs tool (mcp__1a59c906 read) during the Why Project pass by mistake. It was denied with an error and changed nothing. No other non-permitted tools were used.
